AIYANA BROOKS-TAN
[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [PORTFOLIO URL]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Frontend and full-stack developer with internship experience building accessible React components and project experience with TypeScript, Node.js and PostgreSQL. Built and tested a screen-reader-accessible web application as a final-year project. Experience includes freelance web development, automated testing and supporting first-year web development students.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Frontend: React, TypeScript, JavaScript, Next.js, Tailwind CSS
Backend and data: Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, public API integration
Accessibility and testing: Screen-reader testing with NVDA and VoiceOver, Jest, React Testing Library, Lighthouse
Other: Storybook, Firebase Authentication, Chart.js, Vercel, Markdown

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Software Development Intern | Harbourline Media | May 2024–August 2024
- Made accessibility fixes and built components for a React news site.
- Developed a keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery for article pages and documented it in Storybook, using Jest and React Testing Library.

Freelance Web Developer | Yoga Studio Booking Site | 2025
- Built marketing pages and a class timetable with booking requests sent by email.
- Used Next.js static generation and Tailwind CSS, deployed the site on Vercel and maintained content in Markdown files.

Teaching Assistant, First-Year Web Development Lab | Spring 2025
- Supported approximately 30 students over one semester.

Barista | Part-time throughout college

PROJECTS

Tidewatch | Final-Year Project | 2024–2025
- Built an accessible web app displaying tides, water temperature and weather for sea swimmers around the Irish coast.
- Developed a React and TypeScript frontend and a Node.js/Express API that cached data from public weather and tide APIs; used PostgreSQL for user favourites.
- Tested with NVDA and VoiceOver; achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100.
- Received 82% (First Class) and demonstrated the project at the college showcase.
- Technologies included Chart.js and Jest.

Transit Delay Notifier | Student Hackathon | 2024
- Built the frontend in a team of three, creating the notifier in 24 hours and placing second.

Study Buddy | Group Project | 2023
- Built the React frontend and login screens for a study-matching app in a team of four. Other team members developed the API and database.
- Used JavaScript and Firebase Authentication.

EDUCATION
Liffey Institute of Technology
Computing

VOLUNTEERING
Social media volunteer | Sea swimming club

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, concise, readable, and professionally targeted toward frontend/full-stack web development. It presents strong evidence of accessibility work, React/TypeScript projects, Node.js/PostgreSQL project experience, automated testing, Next.js, and Storybook. The strongest evidence includes the accessible gallery, Tidewatch, the Lighthouse score of 100, the 82% final-year grade, and the hackathon result. However, the document slightly overstates the candidate's professional seniority by opening with “Frontend and full-stack developer” despite the original information stating there is no backend job experience and only limited professional experience overall. The Education entry is incomplete, the contact details remain placeholders, and several experience bullets lack useful scope or outcome detail.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The single-column section structure, standard headings, reverse-chronological experience, and conventional skill categories should parse well in most ATS platforms. The CV includes many relevant terms from the advert, including React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Next.js, accessibility, Jest, React Testing Library, Storybook, and Vercel. Its likely AI/ATS screening probability is moderate to good for junior or graduate-level React roles, but lower for this specific advert because it does not show 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience, Git, semantic HTML, responsive design, end-to-end testing, web security, or privacy awareness. “Public API integration” is useful but less directly searchable than “third-party API integration.” The placeholders “[EMAIL],” “[PHONE],” and “[PORTFOLIO URL]” must be replaced before submission because they may reduce both parsing quality and recruiter confidence.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns particularly well with Verdane Care's accessibility and patient-facing product focus. Tidewatch demonstrates accessible user-facing software, React/TypeScript, Node.js/Express, PostgreSQL, API integration, testing, and a wellness-adjacent context through sea swimming. The Yoga Studio booking site provides relevant Next.js and booking-related experience, while the internship provides professional React, accessibility, Storybook, Jest, and React Testing Library experience. Teaching approximately 30 students also supports the advert's mentoring preference. The major factual gap is the requirement for 2+ years of professional React and TypeScript experience: the candidate's material supports an internship and freelance/project work, but not two years of professional experience. Other gaps are end-to-end testing, Git-based workflows, OWASP/web-security awareness, health-data privacy, AWS/Docker, German or Croatian, and analytics/A/B testing. The document should not imply that these gaps are satisfied. It is a credible junior/early-career match with strong accessibility alignment, but not a complete match for the stated must-have profile.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES / HIGH-PRIORITY FIXES
1. Replace the contact placeholders at the top of the CV: change “[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [PORTFOLIO URL]” to the candidate’s actual professional email address, phone number, and portfolio URL. Do not submit the CV with bracketed placeholders.
2. In the Professional Summary, change “Frontend and full-stack developer” to a more accurate formulation such as “Frontend-focused developer with full-stack project experience” or “Frontend developer with React/TypeScript experience and full-stack project experience.” This preserves the Node.js/PostgreSQL evidence without implying two years of professional backend employment.
3. In the Education section, replace the bare “Computing” entry with the exact qualification title and dates only if those details are available in the candidate’s records. Do not invent a degree type, graduation date, or classification.
4. In the Software Development Intern entry, make the professional scope clearer by changing the first bullet to something like “Implemented accessibility fixes and built React components for Harbourline Media’s news site.” This is more specific and uses the job advert’s terminology without adding unsupported claims.
5. In the Teaching Assistant entry, expand the existing bullet using the supported figure: change “Supported approximately 30 students over one semester” to “Supported approximately 30 first-year students during a one-semester web development lab, helping them with web development exercises and troubleshooting.” Do not add teaching activities that did not occur.
6. In the Transit Delay Notifier project, make the outcome and contribution more searchable by changing the bullet to: “Built the frontend in a three-person team during a 24-hour student hackathon; the project placed second.” This accurately captures the candidate’s role and result.

MINOR / TARGETED ENHANCEMENTS
7. In the Technical Skills section, change “public API integration” to “third-party/public API integration” if accurate, reflecting the weather and tide API work in Tidewatch and matching the advert’s integration language.
8. In the Tidewatch project, retain the existing accessibility evidence but make the testing wording more ATS-readable: change “Tested with NVDA and VoiceOver” to “Performed screen-reader testing with NVDA and VoiceOver; achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100.”
9. In the Skills section, keep “Firebase Authentication” under a clearly labelled authentication or application-development category rather than presenting it as evidence of broader web-security expertise. Do not add OWASP, GDPR, Git, Playwright, AWS, Docker, or end-to-end testing because they are not supported by the original candidate information.
10. In the Freelance Web Developer entry, explicitly retain “React” alongside Next.js if the site used React, for example: “Built React/Next.js marketing pages and a class timetable...” This is supported by the portfolio information and improves matching for the role’s core React requirement.
11. In the Experience and Projects sections, use consistent date formatting, such as “May 2024–Aug 2024” and “2024–2025,” throughout. Keep the current standard section headings and avoid tables, text boxes, icons, graphics, or multi-column formatting.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, well-structured junior developer CV with strong evidence of accessibility, React, TypeScript, Node.js, PostgreSQL, testing, and project delivery. The Tidewatch project is particularly effective because it includes a concrete result, an accessibility score, technologies, and an academic grade. The document is truthful against the supplied candidate information; no unsupported skills or experiences were detected. The main content limitations are that the professional experience is relatively short, some bullets are brief or generic, and the education entry is incomplete. The summary could also distinguish more clearly between professional experience and project-based full-stack experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, readable text, simple bullet points, and ATS-friendly formatting. It contains important target keywords including React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Next.js, accessibility, Jest, React Testing Library, Storybook, and Vercel. Its AI/ATS screening probability is moderate to good for junior React/full-stack roles, but weaker for this particular vacancy because the CV does not show Git, semantic HTML, responsive design, end-to-end testing, web security or OWASP awareness, health-data privacy, or 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience. Do not add these keywords unless the candidate can substantiate them. The absence of contact details and links also reduces practical recruiter usability if they are not supplied elsewhere.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with Verdane Care's accessibility-focused, patient-facing product environment. The Tidewatch project demonstrates accessible user-facing software, public API integration, Node.js/Express, PostgreSQL, automated testing, and screen-reader testing. The yoga booking site provides relevant wellness and booking-related experience, while Storybook is a direct match for a nice-to-have requirement. The candidate's teaching-assistant experience also provides some evidence of mentoring potential. However, the candidate's material does not demonstrate the required 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience, end-to-end testing, Git-based workflows, semantic HTML and responsive-layout knowledge, OWASP/web-security awareness, or health-data privacy experience. It also does not show German or Croatian, AWS/Docker, or analytics/A/B testing. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than defects that can be solved through CV wording.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. [High priority — positioning] In the Professional Summary, change the opening from "Frontend and full-stack developer with internship experience" to wording that clearly separates professional and project experience, for example: "Frontend developer with professional internship and freelance experience, plus full-stack project experience using React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL." This avoids implying 2+ years of professional full-stack experience while preserving the strongest relevant evidence.

2. [High priority — missing supported requirement] In the Technical Skills section, add a separate Languages line: "Languages: English — Fluent." The supplied original application is written in fluent English, but the current CV does not state this explicitly.

3. [Medium priority — specificity] In the Professional Experience section under "Software Development Intern | Harbourline Media," change "Made accessibility fixes and built components for a React news site" to "Implemented accessibility fixes and built React components for a news site." Retain the following gallery bullet, which provides the stronger evidence of keyboard accessibility, screen-reader support, Storybook documentation, Jest, and React Testing Library.

4. [Medium priority — completeness] In the Education section, expand "Computing" to "Computing — Third-year student" if this remains factually current for the application. Include the qualification type or expected completion date only if it is known and accurate; do not invent either detail.

5. [Medium priority — recruiter usability] At the top of the CV, include the candidate's actual email address, phone number, LinkedIn URL, and portfolio/GitHub or live-project URL if available. Do not create or imply any link that has not been provided.

6. [Minor] In the Projects section under "Transit Delay Notifier," make the candidate's contribution more ATS-readable by changing "Built the frontend in a team of three" to "Built the frontend in a three-person team for a 24-hour student hackathon; placed second." This preserves the existing facts while making the individual contribution and result easier to scan.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, concise, well structured, and professionally written. It presents a coherent early-career frontend/full-stack profile, with particularly strong evidence of accessibility, React, TypeScript, Node.js, PostgreSQL, and testing experience. The project descriptions are more impactful than the employment bullets because they explain the technology and outcomes. The main content limitation is that the Education entry is too sparse, and some bullets could more explicitly describe the candidate's contribution and technical scope. The CV also accurately presents student, internship, freelance, and project experience without overstating professional seniority.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The conventional section headings, reverse-chronological experience layout, plain text formatting, and standard technology names should parse well in ATS systems. Relevant keywords include React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Next.js, accessibility, Jest, React Testing Library, NVDA, VoiceOver, Storybook, and Vercel. AI screening probability is moderate to good for junior React/full-stack searches, but lower for this specific role because the CV does not demonstrate 2+ years of professional experience, Git-based workflows, end-to-end testing, web security fundamentals, semantic HTML, or responsive design. Do not add unsupported keywords such as Git, Playwright, OWASP, Docker, AWS, or GDPR merely to improve ATS matching.

Tidewatch is especially relevant to Verdane Care's patient-focused and accessibility-oriented culture because it is an accessible user-facing application using external APIs and persistent user data. The candidate's accessibility evidence is unusually strong for an early-career applicant, including NVDA, VoiceOver, and a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100. The material does not establish 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience; the backend experience is project-based rather than professional; and it does not establish end-to-end testing, Git workflows, OWASP/web-security awareness, health-data privacy knowledge, German/Croatian, or healthcare/regulated-environment experience. The yoga studio project supports wellness-related experience, but not healthcare experience.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the Education section, expand the single-line entry to reflect the supported student status and institution more clearly, for example: "Liffey Institute of Technology — Computing student". Include "third-year" only if it is still current.
2. In the Software Development Intern entry, make the testing scope more explicit without implying end-to-end testing. For example, change the second bullet to: "Developed a keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery for article pages, documented it in Storybook, and wrote Jest and React Testing Library unit/component tests." This uses terminology supported by the candidate's portfolio.
3. In the Tidewatch project, make the SQL experience easier for ATS and recruiters to identify by revising the backend/data bullet to: "Developed a React and TypeScript frontend and a Node.js/Express API that cached data from public weather and tide APIs; used PostgreSQL as the SQL database for user favourites." 
4. In the Professional Summary, replace "professional internship and freelance experience, plus full-stack project experience" with a more precise early-career description such as: "Early-career frontend/full-stack developer with internship and freelance web-development experience, plus full-stack academic project experience using React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL." This avoids any possible impression that the candidate already has two years of professional full-stack experience while retaining the strongest supported keywords.
